cards.explanation: The answer is all the days of Jehoiada the priest. The text says Joash did what was right “…all the days of Jehoiada the priest.” That's Jehoiada, the priest who crowned him (2 Chronicles 23:11). I think a young king leaned on that man a lot, friends.
The answer is repairing the house of the LORD. The text says Joash “…set his heart on repairing the house of the LORD.” Set his heart, friends. That's not a passing idea, that's a king who means it.

The answer is False. Joash says, “Do it quickly.” and then the text says, “The Levites, however, did not make haste.” That one little word "however" turns the whole verse around. It's like a friend who says "two minutes!" and then sits back down on the couch.

The answer is True. Joash asks about “…the tax imposed by Moses the servant of the LORD and by the assembly of Israel for the Tent of the Testimony?” Moses is Israel's leader, so this tax goes way back. Joash isn't making up a new rule here, friends.

The answer is that they broke in and used its sacred objects for the Baals. The text says the sons of Athaliah, the wicked woman, “…had broken into the house of God and had even used the sacred objects of the house of the LORD for the Baals.” Baals were false gods. I think this one stings, friends, because those objects belonged to the LORD's house.

The answer is gate. The chest is made at the king's command and “…placed outside, at the gate of the house of the LORD.” Not inside, but outside at the gate. A chest, a gate and a king's command, friends.

The answer is rejoice. The text says, “All the officers and all the people rejoiced and brought their contributions, and they dropped them in the chest until it was full.” They didn't just give, they were glad about it. That's a full chest and a full heart.

The answer is day. The text says the royal scribe and the high priest's officer would come and empty the chest and carry it back to its place, and “They did this daily…” Every single day, friends. That's a very regular schedule.

The answer is stonecutters and carpenters and metalworkers. The text says the money was used “…to hire stonecutters and carpenters to restore the house of the LORD, as well as workers in iron and bronze to repair the house of the LORD.” Stone, wood, iron and bronze. That's a full crew for a big repair.

The answer is True. The text says, “They restored the house of God according to its specifications, and they reinforced it.” They followed the plan, and they reinforced it too. I think that's a job done with care, friends.

The answer is that the leftover money is used to make articles for the house of the LORD. The text says, “When they were finished, they brought the rest of the money to the king and Jehoiada, and with it were made articles for the house of the LORD…” Jehoiada is the priest who, with the king, gave the money to the supervisors in verse 12. The leftovers went right back into the LORD's house.

The answer is regularly. The text says, “Throughout the days of Jehoiada, burnt offerings were presented regularly in the house of the LORD.” The house was repaired, and the offerings were presented regularly. That's steady worship, friends, like an oven you can count on.
The answer is 130. The text says, “When Jehoiada was old and full of years, he died at the age of 130.” Full of years is a lovely way to put it. I think this is a tender moment, so let's let it be.

The answer is that he did what was good in Israel for God and His temple. The text says Jehoiada “…was buried with the kings in the City of David, because he had done what was good in Israel for God and His temple.” Jehoiada is called the high priest in verse 6, and still he was buried with the kings. The text gives the reason right there in the verse.
